ledger.x: c. 210: Bhima-naga rules the Nagas from Padmavati after the Kushan decline. "Bhima-naga, r. c. 210-230 CE", probably the first to rule from Padmavati; "The Nagas rose to power after the decline of the Kushan Empire in north-central India, in the early 3rd century." The year is the page's (c.); the extent is Trivedi's…
Page silent on the year: the Naga rule extends north to Mathura.
Page silent on the year: the Naga rule extends south to Ujjain.

c. 347: Samudragupta defeats Ganapati-naga and the Naga lands pass to the Guptas. "The Allahabad Pillar inscription of the Gupta king Samudragupta states that he defeated Ganapati-naga" (Nagas page); the Samudragupta page lists Ganapati-naga and Nagasena among the eight kings of Aryavarta and says their kingdoms "were…
c. 347: the Naga dynasty ends. "This suggests that Ganapati-naga was the last Naga king" and the page puts the end in the mid-4th century with no exact year.

wars.name: Samudragupta's campaign against the kings of Aryavarta
wars.outcome: Gupta victory: Ganapati-naga and Nagasena among the eight kings of Aryavarta "uprooted"; their kingdoms annexed to the Gupta empire.

certainty.note: No border is given by any page; the extent follows coin finds (Pawaya, Narwar, Gohad, Vidisha, Kutwar, Ujjain, Mathura, Jhansi).
